screening_decisions.reason: This study compares vecuronium, atracurium, and rocuronium without any sugammadex intervention. Does not meet the inclusion criteria as sugammadex is not studied.
Randomized trial comparing different doses of rocuronium only. No sugammadex is involved in this study. Does not meet inclusion criteria.

RCT using sugammadex (2 mg/kg) for reversal of rocuronium-induced neuromuscular block in adult surgical patients. While the primary comparison is between propofol and sevoflurane anesthesia, sugammadex is the intervention being evaluated in adult patients meeting the inclusion criteria.
Study uses pyridostigmine for reversal, not sugammadex. No sugammadex intervention is present. Does not meet inclusion criteria.
Survey study evaluating changes in management practices over time. Not a randomized controlled trial. Wrong study design.

RCT comparing sugammadex (4 mg/kg) with neostigmine-glycopyrrolate and edrophonium-atropine in 60 adult surgical patients. Directly meets inclusion criteria as sugammadex is compared with other reversal medications.
Review article summarizing Phase I-III trials of sugammadex. Not a primary randomized controlled trial. Wrong study design.
Review article discussing residual neuromuscular blockade. Not a primary randomized controlled trial. Wrong study design.
Study examining atracurium and postoperative residual curarization. No sugammadex intervention. Does not meet inclusion criteria.
RCT with 102 adult surgical patients (age 21-64) receiving different doses of sugammadex (0.5 to 8.0 mg/kg). Directly meets inclusion criteria as different doses of sugammadex are compared.
Survey study covering 12 UK anaesthetic departments. Not a randomized controlled trial. Wrong study design.

Randomized multicentre parallel-group trial with 100 adult surgical patients (age ≥20) receiving sugammadex (0.5, 1.0, 2.0, or 4.0 mg/kg) or placebo. Meets inclusion criteria as sugammadex is compared with placebo and different doses are tested.
Study conducted in 10 awake healthy volunteers, not adult surgical patients. Also no sugammadex intervention. Excluded per criteria excluding healthy volunteers.
Methodological paper on meta-analysis statistics. Not a clinical trial. Wrong study design.
Phase I study conducted in healthy volunteers (12 subjects). Explicitly excluded per selection criteria which states 'studies on healthy volunteers' should be excluded.
RCT comparing cisatracurium and rocuronium. No sugammadex intervention. Does not meet inclusion criteria.
RCT comparing pancuronium, atracurium, and vecuronium. No sugammadex intervention. Does not meet inclusion criteria.
Methodological review article on meta-analysis methods. Not a primary clinical trial. Wrong study design.
RCT studying atracurium and neostigmine effects on depth of anaesthesia. No sugammadex intervention. Does not meet inclusion criteria.

Phase III RCT with 30 adult patients (15 renally impaired, 15 controls) receiving sugammadex (2.0 mg/kg) for reversal of rocuronium-induced neuromuscular block. Meets inclusion criteria as sugammadex is studied in adult patients.
This is a review article discussing ventilation and residual effects of neuromuscular blocking drugs and volatile anesthetics. It is not an RCT and does not involve sugammadex.
This is a review/educational article about detection and criteria for postoperative residual curarization. It is not an RCT and does not involve sugammadex.
This is an overview article providing general knowledge on neuromuscular blocking agents during anesthesia. It is not an RCT and does not involve sugammadex.
This is a systematic review about the impact of grey literature in meta-analyses. It is not an RCT and does not involve sugammadex or neuromuscular blockade.
This is a methodological study about detecting bias in meta-analyses using funnel plots. It is not an RCT and does not involve sugammadex.

This is an RCT with 20 adult patients (20-81 years, ASA 1-2) who were randomly assigned to different doses of sugammadex (1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 6.0, 8.0 mg/kg) for reversal of pancuronium-induced neuromuscular block. Meets criteria as it compares different doses of sugammadex in adult patients.
This is an observational case-control study assessing TOF ratios in patients with critical respiratory events versus matched controls. It is not an RCT and does not involve sugammadex.
This is a prospective observational study examining risk factors for complications and mortality following anesthesia. It is not an RCT and does not involve sugammadex.

This is a randomized Phase II dose-finding study with 50 adult patients randomized to different doses of sugammadex (0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, or 8.0 mg/kg) for reversal of rocuronium-induced neuromuscular block. Meets criteria as it compares different doses of sugammadex in adult patients.

This is an RCT with 30 anesthetized adult patients who received randomly assigned doses of sugammadex (Org 25969) at 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, or 6.0 mg/kg for reversal of prolonged rocuronium-induced neuromuscular block. Meets criteria as it compares different doses of sugammadex in adult patients.
This is a review/commentary article discussing findings from previous investigators about residual paralysis and neostigmine-assisted antagonism. It is not an RCT and does not involve sugammadex.

This is a randomized, safety-assessor-blinded study with 84 adult surgical patients (ASA I-III) comparing sugammadex 2.0 mg/kg for reversal of rocuronium-induced block with neostigmine 50 µg/kg for reversal of cisatracurium-induced block. Meets criteria as it compares sugammadex with another medication (neostigmine) in adult patients.
This is an RCT comparing different neuromuscular blocking agents (rocuronium, succinylcholine, vecuronium) for rapid-sequence induction. It does not involve sugammadex as an intervention.
This is an animal study conducted in dogs, not human patients. It does not involve sugammadex and does not meet the population criteria.
This is a case report with pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modeling based on a single patient case. It is not an RCT.
This is an observational survey study assessing incidence of postoperative residual curarization following atracurium or vecuronium. It is not an RCT and does not involve sugammadex.
This is a methodological/statistical paper about a rank correlation test for detecting publication bias in meta-analyses. It is not an RCT and does not involve sugammadex.

This is a randomized, multicentre, parallel-group trial with 98 adult subjects (age ≥18 years, ASA 1-3) comparing sugammadex 2.0 mg/kg with neostigmine 50 µg/kg plus glycopyrrolate for reversal of rocuronium-induced neuromuscular blockade. Meets criteria as it compares sugammadex with another medication in adult patients.
This is an observational study assessing residual neuromuscular blockade in 64 PACU patients using low-current TOF stimulation. It is not an RCT and does not involve sugammadex.
